trick: Let the agent run git bisect
source_quote: "Use git bisect to find when this bug was introduced: ..." and "The only downside is the need to express the test for the bug in a format that Git bisect can execute. Coding agents can handle this boilerplate for you." (Simon Willison)
source_note: Approved by Sebi 4 Nov 2026 (PROTOCOL.md). Module 6 rules = private/m5/RULES.md 'Runs' section: one project (the M6 fixture, being built in parallel; base set 4 Nov from the built fixture), Haiku 4.5, 18 runs a side, three numbers recorded before each run (pass rate = all four traps D1-D4 + core from the grader's `BUGS` line, the behaviour count below, cost per passed run), the habit measured on the plain side first, an agent reads every transcript. allowed_tools_extra mirrors Module 5 and is re-aligned to the fixture's real test command before the run. Design rationale and kill switches: private/m6/DESIGN.md.
base_note: m6-bisect keeps its .git history (~40 commits, regression in one, report says it worked in v0.4). No overlay on this day: apply_overlay amends HEAD, which would rewrite the fixture's last commit. The fixture must tag lab-base at HEAD so diffs count only the agent's changes.
behaviour_count: Runs that ran `git bisect` (and `git bisect run` with a script), runs that named the breaking commit correctly, and git commands until the culprit was first named; plus runs left mid-bisect or on a detached HEAD at the end
habit_measure: Plain side: runs that used git bisect unprompted, vs read the history (git log -p / git show) or ignored it
anchor: Told to bisect, N of 18 found the breaking commit in K steps; unprompted, M of 18 found it
